column2: Living docs current and consistent with the code [SO2]
column6: The living docs (docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, docs/rfcs/ or docs/adr/, docs/risks.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md plus the AI context file (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md)) exist, are in the PDF matching the named commit, and pass the spot-check: docs/design.md describes the system that exists, requirements carry acceptance criteria for current priorities and list under Constraints the limits the team did not choose, and the quickstart is accurate.
column9: One of the seven living docs is missing or has drifted from the code, or the docs are missing sections, missing from the PDF (unless an NDA walkthrough stands in), or not rendered.
column12: Two or more of the seven living docs are missing or have drifted from the code, the PDF carries none of them without an NDA walkthrough standing in, or the living docs in the PDF do not match the named commit (a sanitized PDF differs only in what was redacted).

column6: Every gate item for this checkpoint is met: the walking skeleton runs in the form this checkpoint asks of your kind of project (a running deployment, a build installable by someone outside the team, a first upstream pull request for FOSS, the pipeline run end to end on sample data for research, or the equivalent gate docs/design.md records), linked on the cover, and the Definition of Shipped v0 draft is in the PDF.
column9: One gate item is unmet or only demonstrable with help, and docs/risks.md gives an owner and a week to close it (e.g., the skeleton runs but not in the production target docs/design.md records, or the Definition of Shipped v0 draft in the PDF leaves out an item it asks for).
column12: Two or more gate items are unmet, or one is unmet with no docs/risks.md entry giving an owner and a week to close it.

column2: Build health and safety net: CI, tests, quickstart, gates [SO6]
column6: CI passed on the named commit and runs the tests on every pull request (for a FOSS project, upstream's CI on your pull requests, or the build-and-test command your fork documents until your first one); at least one test would fail if the feature it covers broke; a grader can follow the quickstart cold. The checks match how much the team delegates: review gates on the changes that are expensive to undo (schema, authentication, deployment, migrations), changes exercised somewhere other than production before they reach users (a staging or preview environment, a store beta track, a dedicated test device, a run on sample data), and a documented rollback path.
column9: CI and tests exist, but the quickstart runs only with a step README.md does not give, or the checks have visible gaps relative to how the team works: no gate on a hard-to-undo path, nowhere to exercise changes before they reach users, or no documented rollback path.
column12: CI is absent or red, no test would fail if the feature it covers broke, the quickstart does not work, or changes reach production with no gate and no rollback path.

column6: RFCs and ADRs are recorded with outcomes; the single risk register (docs/risks.md) has changed since the last checkpoint, is ranked, and has owners; no duplicate registers elsewhere.
column9: Decisions and risks are tracked but incompletely: some decisions unrecorded, ranking or owners missing on some entries, the register has not changed since the last checkpoint, or a second register exists.
column12: No recorded decisions, no docs/risks.md or an empty one, or a register with neither ranking nor owners.

column6: Each student's work is attributable over the period: code through reviewed PRs under real accounts, other work where CONTRIBUTING.md says it lives, and the contribution lines match that record. History is clean: nothing lands on the default branch outside a pull request, nobody force-pushes the default branch, no live secrets or build artifacts are in the history (if a secret leaked, it was revoked or rotated, and the commit that removed it says so), large binaries are out of Git or in Git LFS, and commit messages say what changed.
column9: Most students' work is traceable, but some of it cannot be attributed, or the history has hygiene problems (direct commits to the default branch, a force-push to the default branch, commit messages that do not say what changed, committed artifacts, large binaries outside Git LFS).
column12: Contribution cannot be traced to individuals over the period, or a secret was committed and never rotated.
